events.title: Three Mile Island Nuclear Accident
events.description: A partial meltdown of the Unit 2 reactor at the Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station near Harrisburg, Pennsylvania, began after a cooling system malfunction and operator errors. A small amount of radioactive gas was released into the environment.
events.significance: It was the most serious accident in U.S. commercial nuclear power history, leading to stricter safety regulations and oversight and contributing to a decline in new nuclear plant construction in the United States.

events.title: Death of Virginia Woolf
events.description: English novelist and essayist Virginia Woolf died by suicide, drowning in the River Ouse near her home in Sussex, England, after long struggles with mental illness.
events.significance: Woolf was a leading modernist writer whose works, including Mrs Dalloway, To the Lighthouse and A Room of One's Own, shaped modern literature and feminist thought.

events.title: Britain and France Declare War on Russia
events.description: The United Kingdom and France formally declared war on the Russian Empire, joining the Ottoman Empire in the conflict over Russian ambitions and influence in the Black Sea region and the Balkans.
events.significance: This marked their formal entry into the Crimean War, which reshaped the balance of power in Europe and exposed military and medical shortcomings, prompting reforms such as those championed by Florence Nightingale.

events.title: Constantinople and Angora Officially Renamed Istanbul and Ankara
events.description: The Turkish Postal Service Law took effect, requiring international use of Turkish names Istanbul and Ankara for the cities previously known in the West as Constantinople and Angora.
events.significance: The change was part of Atatürk's modernization and nationalization reforms, reinforcing the new Turkish Republic's identity.

events.title: Death of Dwight D. Eisenhower
events.description: Dwight D. Eisenhower, the 34th President of the United States and Supreme Allied Commander in Europe during World War II, died at Walter Reed Army Medical Center in Washington, D.C.
events.significance: Eisenhower led the Allied invasion of Normandy and as president oversaw the end of the Korean War and the creation of the Interstate Highway System, and he warned of the military-industrial complex.
